claim: Gαq protein is expressed in human endometrium during the mid-proliferative phase, mid-secretory phase, and in decidual tissue of early pregnancy.
source: The positive expression of Gαq showed in the endometrium of mid-proliferative, mid-secretary phase, and decidual tissue of early pregnancy (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A demonstrates Gαq expression in these tissue types.

claim: Gαq expression is higher in stromal cells at mid-secretory phase during the menstrual cycle.
source: Expression of Gαq was higher in stromal cell at mid-secretary phase during menstrual cycle, which is the timing for implantation (implantation windows), and in deciduas of early pregnancy (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A shows higher Gαq expression in stromal cells during mid-secretory phase.

claim: Gαq expression increases significantly in human endometrial stromal cells as differentiation progresses over time in vitro.
source: As shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C, the expression of both the Gαq transcript and protein increased significantly in the HESC as the differentiation progressed over time in vitro.
evidence: qRT-PCR and western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C demonstrate increased Gαq expression during differentiation.

claim: Gαq is expressed in both cytoplasm and nucleus of proliferative and differentiated human endometrial stromal cells.
source: As shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, E, Gαq was expressed in both cytoplasm and nucleus of proliferative and differentiated cells.
evidence: Immunofluorescence and subcellular fraction experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, E demonstrate Gαq localization in both compartments.

claim: GNAQ knockout in HESC results in decreased Ki67 expression on the first day of decidual induction.
source: It showed no significant change in control (CON) and GNAQ-KO HESC in the proliferative state, but remarkable decrease in GNAQ-KO cells on the first day of decidua induction (Figure 1A).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data in Figure 1A shows decreased Ki67 in GNAQ-KO cells at day 1 of differentiation.

claim: GNAQ knockout significantly accelerates the expression of PRL mRNA during decidualization.
source: Meanwhile, compared with control decidual cells, GNAQ-KO significantly accelerated the expression of PRL and IGFBP1 mRNA (Figure 1B, C).
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 1B shows increased PRL mRNA in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.

claim: GNAQ knockout significantly accelerates the expression of IGFBP1 mRNA during decidualization.
source: Meanwhile, compared with control decidual cells, GNAQ-KO significantly accelerated the expression of PRL and IGFBP1 mRNA (Figure 1B, C).
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 1C shows increased IGFBP1 mRNA in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.

claim: IGFBP1 protein level is significantly increased upon Gαq deficiency in decidual cells.
source: Consistently, the level of IGFBP1 protein was also increased significantly upon Gαq deficiency (Figure 1D).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 1D demonstrates increased IGFBP1 protein in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.

claim: More than 3880 genes were altered in GNAQ knockout decidual cells compared to control.
source: More than 3880 genes were altered in the absence of GNAQ (Figure 1E).
evidence: RNA-seq data shown in volcano plot in Figure 1E identifies differentially expressed genes.

claim: KEGG analysis revealed that Wnt signaling pathway is among the top-ranked biological processes altered in GNAQ knockout decidual cells.
source: Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis revealed that most top-ranked biological processes included the Wnt signaling pathway (Sharma et al., 2016; Pathak et al., 2021) and JAK–STAT, NF-κB inflammation pathway (Figure 1F, G), which had been reported to regulate stromal apoptosis and differentiation during the decidualization, the latter consistent with the notions regarding the role of Gαq during immune regulation (Wang et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: KEGG pathway analysis in Figure 1F, G shows enrichment of Wnt signaling pathway, supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: KEGG analysis revealed that JAK-STAT and NF-κB inflammation pathways are among the top-ranked biological processes altered in GNAQ knockout decidual cells.
source: Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis revealed that most top-ranked biological processes included the Wnt signaling pathway (Sharma et al., 2016; Pathak et al., 2021) and JAK–STAT, NF-κB inflammation pathway (Figure 1F, G), which had been reported to regulate stromal apoptosis and differentiation during the decidualization, the latter consistent with the notions regarding the role of Gαq during immune regulation (Wang et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: KEGG pathway analysis in Figure 1F, G shows enrichment of JAK-STAT and NF-κB pathways, supported by citations to previous studies on their role in decidualization and immune regulation.

claim: Nuclear translocation of NF-κB subunits p65 and p50 is higher in GNAQ-KO decidual cells than in control.
source: As shown in Figure 2A–C, Figure 2—figure supplements 1A and 2A–C, nuclear translocation and phosphorylation of the NF-κB subunits p65 and p50 were higher in GNAQ-KO decidual cells than in control.
evidence: Western blot and immunofluorescence data in Figure 2A-C and supplements show increased nuclear p65 and p50 in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: Phosphorylation of NF-κB subunits p65 and p50 is higher in GNAQ-KO decidual cells than in control.
source: As shown in Figure 2A–C, Figure 2—figure supplements 1A and 2A–C, nuclear translocation and phosphorylation of the NF-κB subunits p65 and p50 were higher in GNAQ-KO decidual cells than in control.
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 2C and supplements show increased phosphorylation of p65 in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: IL-11 mRNA expression is significantly upregulated in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: As show in Figure 2, there is a significant upregulation of interlukin-11 (IL-11) (Figure 2D) and interlukin-1β (IL-1β) (Figure 2E) in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 2D shows increased IL-11 mRNA in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.

claim: IL-1β mRNA expression is significantly upregulated in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: As show in Figure 2, there is a significant upregulation of interlukin-11 (IL-11) (Figure 2D) and interlukin-1β (IL-1β) (Figure 2E) in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 2E shows increased IL-1β mRNA in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.

claim: IL-1β protein levels are significantly increased upon Gαq deficiency in decidual cells.
source: Consistently, the IL-1β protein levels were also significantly increased upon Gαq deficiency in decidual cells (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 2F and supplement 2E shows increased IL-1β protein in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.

claim: Phosphorylated STAT3 is the activated form of STAT3 and is the convergent downstream effector of IL-11 signaling.
source: STAT3 is maximally expressed in decidual cells during late-secretory phase (Dimitriadis et al., 2006), phosphorylated STAT3 is the activated form of STAT3 and is the convergent downstream effector of IL-11 (Taniguchi and Karin, 2014; Heichler et al., 2020) and IL-1β (Yao et al., 2017) signaling.
evidence: Statement is supported by citations to previous studies on STAT3 activation by IL-11.

claim: Phosphorylated STAT3 is the convergent downstream effector of IL-1β signaling.
source: STAT3 is maximally expressed in decidual cells during late-secretory phase (Dimitriadis et al., 2006), phosphorylated STAT3 is the activated form of STAT3 and is the convergent downstream effector of IL-11 (Taniguchi and Karin, 2014; Heichler et al., 2020) and IL-1β (Yao et al., 2017) signaling.
evidence: Statement is supported by citation to previous study on STAT3 activation by IL-1β.

claim: Gαq deficiency significantly enhances the phosphorylation of STAT3 in decidual stromal cells.
source: We performed western blot to analyze the STAT3 phosphorylation level in decidual cells upon Gαq knockout, and found that Gαq deficiency could significantly enhance the phosphorylation of STAT3 in DSCs (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 2F and supplement 2D shows increased p-STAT3 in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.

claim: NF-κB inhibitor PDTC reduces the overexpression of IL-11 in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: The treatment of PDTC inhibitor blocked NF-κB translocate to the nucleus (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), reduced the overexpression of IL-11, IL-1β, and also the phosphorylated status of STAT3 (Figure 2G–I and Figure 2—figure supplement 2F, G).
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 2G shows PDTC treatment reduces IL-11 mRNA in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: NF-κB inhibitor PDTC reduces the overexpression of IL-1β in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: The treatment of PDTC inhibitor blocked NF-κB translocate to the nucleus (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), reduced the overexpression of IL-11, IL-1β, and also the phosphorylated status of STAT3 (Figure 2G–I and Figure 2—figure supplement 2F, G).
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 2H shows PDTC treatment reduces IL-1β mRNA in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: NF-κB inhibitor PDTC reduces the phosphorylated status of STAT3 in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: The treatment of PDTC inhibitor blocked NF-κB translocate to the nucleus (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), reduced the overexpression of IL-11, IL-1β, and also the phosphorylated status of STAT3 (Figure 2G–I and Figure 2—figure supplement 2F, G).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 2I and supplement 2F shows PDTC treatment reduces p-STAT3 in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: NF-κB inhibitor PDTC slows down the advanced expression of decidual markers PRL and IGFBP-1 in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: Meanwhile, the NF-κB inhibitor slowed down the advanced expression of decidual markers PRL and IGFBP-1 in GNAQ-KO decidual cells (Figure 2J–L and Figure 2—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: qRT-PCR and western blot data in Figure 2J-L and supplement 2H show PDTC treatment reduces PRL and IGFBP-1 expression in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: Gαq modulates the expression of inflammatory cytokines by inhibiting over-activation of NF-κB signaling pathway during decidualization.
source: Collectively, Gαq modulated the expression of inflammatory cytokine by inhibiting over-activation of NF-κB signaling pathway during decidualization.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the experimental data showing that Gαq deficiency leads to increased NF-κB activity and inflammatory cytokine expression, which can be rescued by NF-κB inhibition.

claim: NFκBIA mRNA levels are significantly attenuated in early GNAQ-KO decidual cells but not in Gαq deficiency proliferative stroma compared with control cells.
source: Interestingly, we found that both mRNA and protein level of NFκBIA were significantly attenuated in early GNAQ-KO decidual cells, but not in Gαq deficiency proliferative stroma compared with control cells (Figure 3A, B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 3A shows decreased NFκBIA mRNA in GNAQ-KO decidual cells but not in proliferative cells.

claim: NFκBIA protein levels are significantly attenuated in early GNAQ-KO decidual cells but not in Gαq deficiency proliferative stroma compared with control cells.
source: Interestingly, we found that both mRNA and protein level of NFκBIA were significantly attenuated in early GNAQ-KO decidual cells, but not in Gαq deficiency proliferative stroma compared with control cells (Figure 3A, B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 3B and supplement 1A shows decreased IκBα protein in GNAQ-KO decidual cells but not in proliferative cells.

claim: There is no obvious difference in the ratio of phosphorylated IκBα in GNAQ-KO decidual cells compared to control.
source: However, there is no obvious difference of ratio of phosphorylated IκBα in GNAQ-KO decidual cells (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 3B and supplement 1B shows no significant difference in p-IκBα ratio.

claim: Overexpression of IκBα reduces nuclear translocation of NF-κB subunits p65 and p50 in NFκBIA overexpression GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: As expected, nuclear translocation of the NF-κB subunit p65 and p50 were less in NFκBIA overexpression GNAQ-KO decidual cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data in Figure 3C shows reduced nuclear p65 and p50 upon IκBα overexpression in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: Overexpression of IκBα reduces the phosphorylation of STAT3 in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: Meanwhile, overexpression of the IκBα, but not lentivirus transfected with empty vector reduced the phosphorylation of STAT3 (Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F) and significantly alleviated advanced progression of decidualization in GNAQ-KO decidual cells (Figure 3E, F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 3F and supplement 1F shows reduced p-STAT3 upon IκBα overexpression in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: Overexpression of IκBα significantly alleviates advanced progression of decidualization in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: Meanwhile, overexpression of the IκBα, but not lentivirus transfected with empty vector reduced the phosphorylation of STAT3 (Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F) and significantly alleviated advanced progression of decidualization in GNAQ-KO decidual cells (Figure 3E, F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: qRT-PCR and western blot data in Figure 3E, F and supplement 1E show reduced IGFBP-1 expression upon IκBα overexpression in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: Gαq is detected in the nucleoplasm of decidual stromal cells.
source: To further explore the nuclear role of Gαq, we performed chromatin protein isolation assays and detected Gαq in the nucleoplasm (Figure 4A).
evidence: Chromatin protein isolation assay in Figure 4A shows Gαq presence in nucleoplasm fraction.

claim: Both HA-tagged WT Gαq and NES Gαq can restore NFκBIA expression in Gαq knockout decidual cells.
source: Next, we evaluated the function of Gαq in different compartments by re-expressing HA-tagged WT Gαq (HA-Gαq) or NES Gαq plasmids contained a fused potent nuclear export sequence into Gαq knockout decidual cells (Figure 4B), and found that both of them can restore NFκBIA expression (Figure 4C), downregulated the expression of IL-11, IL-1β, and phosphorylation of STAT3 (Figure 4D–F), and alleviated the advanced progression of decidualization in Gαq deficiency decidual cells (Figure 4F).
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 4C shows both HA-Gαq and GNAQ-NES restore NFκBIA expression in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: Both HA-tagged WT Gαq and NES Gαq downregulate the expression of IL-11 and IL-1β in Gαq knockout decidual cells.
source: Next, we evaluated the function of Gαq in different compartments by re-expressing HA-tagged WT Gαq (HA-Gαq) or NES Gαq plasmids contained a fused potent nuclear export sequence into Gαq knockout decidual cells (Figure 4B), and found that both of them can restore NFκBIA expression (Figure 4C), downregulated the expression of IL-11, IL-1β, and phosphorylation of STAT3 (Figure 4D–F), and alleviated the advanced progression of decidualization in Gαq deficiency decidual cells (Figure 4F).
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 4D-E shows both HA-Gαq and GNAQ-NES reduce IL-11 and IL-1β expression in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: Both HA-tagged WT Gαq and NES Gαq reduce phosphorylation of STAT3 in Gαq knockout decidual cells.
source: Next, we evaluated the function of Gαq in different compartments by re-expressing HA-tagged WT Gαq (HA-Gαq) or NES Gαq plasmids contained a fused potent nuclear export sequence into Gαq knockout decidual cells (Figure 4B), and found that both of them can restore NFκBIA expression (Figure 4C), downregulated the expression of IL-11, IL-1β, and phosphorylation of STAT3 (Figure 4D–F), and alleviated the advanced progression of decidualization in Gαq deficiency decidual cells (Figure 4F).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 4F shows both HA-Gαq and GNAQ-NES reduce p-STAT3 in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: Both HA-tagged WT Gαq and NES Gαq alleviate the advanced progression of decidualization in Gαq deficiency decidual cells.
source: Next, we evaluated the function of Gαq in different compartments by re-expressing HA-tagged WT Gαq (HA-Gαq) or NES Gαq plasmids contained a fused potent nuclear export sequence into Gαq knockout decidual cells (Figure 4B), and found that both of them can restore NFκBIA expression (Figure 4C), downregulated the expression of IL-11, IL-1β, and phosphorylation of STAT3 (Figure 4D–F), and alleviated the advanced progression of decidualization in Gαq deficiency decidual cells (Figure 4F).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 4F shows both HA-Gαq and GNAQ-NES reduce IGFBP-1 expression in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: Cytoplasmic localization of Gαq protein plays a dominant role in inhibiting the overexpression of inflammatory cytokines and directing the progression of decidualization by regulating the expression of NFκBIA.
source: These results suggested that cytoplastic localization of Gαq protein played a dominate role in inhibiting the overexpression of inflammatory cytokine and directing the progression of decidualization by regulating the expression of NFκBIA.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from experiments showing that both cytoplasmic WT Gαq and NES-tagged Gαq (which is exported from nucleus) can rescue the phenotype in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: PKD/PKCμser744/748 phosphorylation level is significantly reduced in Gαq deficiency differentiated stromal cells.
source: As shown in Figure 5, PKD/PKCμser744/748 phosphorylation level was significantly reduced (Figure 5A), but we detected no significant alteration in PKCα/β phosphorylation in Gαq deficiency differentiated stromal cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 5A shows reduced p-PKD/PKCμ in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.

claim: There is no significant alteration in PKCα/β phosphorylation in Gαq deficiency differentiated stromal cells.
source: As shown in Figure 5, PKD/PKCμser744/748 phosphorylation level was significantly reduced (Figure 5A), but we detected no significant alteration in PKCα/β phosphorylation in Gαq deficiency differentiated stromal cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A shows no significant change in p-PKCα/β in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.

claim: PMA at a concentration of 1 nM is able to activate PKD/PKCμ pathway and abolish the aberrant expression of decidual marker IGFBP-1 in Gαq knockout cells.
source: Interestingly, at a concentration of 1 nM, PMA was able to activate PKD/PKCμ pathway and abolished the aberrant expression of decidual marker IGFBP-1 in Gαq knockout cells (Figure 5B), but inhibited the activation of p-PKCα/β in normal decidual cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 5B shows PMA treatment activates PKD/PKCμ and reduces IGFBP-1 in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: PMA at 1 nM concentration has no significant effect on PKA activation.
source: In contrast, PMA had no significant effect on PKA activation at this concentration (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C shows no change in p-PKA upon PMA treatment.

claim: The phosphorylation level of PKA does not respond obviously to Gαq knockout.
source: However, the phosphorylation level of PKA did not respond obviously to Gαq knockout (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D shows no significant change in p-PKA in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: Gαq-mediated HESC decidualization occurs mainly by stimulating PKD/PKCμ activation.
source: Taken together, these results implied that Gαq-mediated HESC decidualization mainly by stimulating the PKD/PKCμ activation.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from data showing PKD/PKCμ phosphorylation is reduced in GNAQ-KO cells and can be rescued by PMA, while PKCα/β and PKA are not significantly affected.

claim: HDAC5 phosphorylation level is significantly reduced in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: To determine the potential mechanism of PKD/PKCμ signaling pathway in regulating the NFκBIA transcription during decidualization, we investigated the phosphorylation level of HDAC5 in GNAQ-KO HESC. As shown in Figure 5A–C, the HDAC5 phosphorylation level was significantly reduced in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 5A-C shows reduced p-HDAC5 in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.

claim: PKD/PKCμ activator PMA dramatically rescues the reduced phosphorylation level of HDAC5 in GNAQ-KO cells.
source: Then, the change was further validated by using the PKD/PKCμ activator and inhibitor during decidualization in GNAQ-KO cells. As expected, the reduced phosphorylation level of HDAC5 upon Gαq knockout was dramatically rescued after activator PMA treatment (Figure 5B, C), and co-treatment with PKD/PKCμ inhibitor, CID755673 blocked the PMA-induced HDAC5 phosphorylation (Figure 5C).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 5B, C shows PMA treatment increases p-HDAC5 in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: PKD/PKCμ inhibitor CID755673 blocks PMA-induced HDAC5 phosphorylation.
source: Then, the change was further validated by using the PKD/PKCμ activator and inhibitor during decidualization in GNAQ-KO cells. As expected, the reduced phosphorylation level of HDAC5 upon Gαq knockout was dramatically rescued after activator PMA treatment (Figure 5B, C), and co-treatment with PKD/PKCμ inhibitor, CID755673 blocked the PMA-induced HDAC5 phosphorylation (Figure 5C).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 5C shows CID755673 treatment blocks PMA-induced p-HDAC5 increase.

claim: PKD/PKCμ regulates HDAC5 phosphorylation status during decidualization.
source: These results suggested that PKD/PKCμ regulated the HDAC5 phosphorylation status during decidualization.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from experiments showing PKD/PKCμ activator increases HDAC5 phosphorylation while inhibitor blocks it.

claim: HDAC5 phosphorylation level in cytoplasm is evidently decreased in GNAQ-KO decidual cells compared with control decidual cells.
source: To prove this assumption, firstly, it showed that evidently decreased HDAC5 phosphorylation level in cytoplasm of GNAQ-KO decidual cells compared with the control decidual cells (Figure 5D, E), and PKD/PKCμ activator, PMA, dramatically reversed the reduced phosphorylation level of HDAC5 in cytoplasm (Figure 5E), further corroborated that the phosphorylated HDAC5 could stimulate its nuclear export.
evidence: Immunofluorescence and western blot data in Figure 5D, E shows decreased cytoplasmic p-HDAC5 in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: PKD/PKCμ activator PMA dramatically reverses the reduced phosphorylation level of HDAC5 in cytoplasm.
source: To prove this assumption, firstly, it showed that evidently decreased HDAC5 phosphorylation level in cytoplasm of GNAQ-KO decidual cells compared with the control decidual cells (Figure 5D, E), and PKD/PKCμ activator, PMA, dramatically reversed the reduced phosphorylation level of HDAC5 in cytoplasm (Figure 5E), further corroborated that the phosphorylated HDAC5 could stimulate its nuclear export.
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 5E shows PMA treatment increases cytoplasmic p-HDAC5.

claim: HDAC5 is enriched in the NFκBIA promoter.
source: Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assay verified the enrichment of HDAC5 in NFκBIA promotor (Figure 5F).
evidence: ChIP-qRT-PCR data in Figure 5F shows HDAC5 enrichment at NFκBIA promoter.

claim: HDAC5 inhibitor LMK235 significantly rescues NFκBIA expression in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: Further study detected NFκBIA expression in GNAQ-KO decidual cells treated with HDAC5 inhibitor, LMK235. As shown in Figure 5G, LMK235 significantly rescued the NFκBIA expression in GNAQ-KO decidual cells, downregulated its effectors IL-11 (Figure 5H) and IL-1β (Figure 5I) expression and alleviated the advanced progression of decidualization (Figure 5J) in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 5G shows LMK235 treatment increases NFκBIA expression in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: HDAC5 inhibitor LMK235 downregulates IL-11 expression in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: Further study detected NFκBIA expression in GNAQ-KO decidual cells treated with HDAC5 inhibitor, LMK235. As shown in Figure 5G, LMK235 significantly rescued the NFκBIA expression in GNAQ-KO decidual cells, downregulated its effectors IL-11 (Figure 5H) and IL-1β (Figure 5I) expression and alleviated the advanced progression of decidualization (Figure 5J) in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 5H shows LMK235 treatment reduces IL-11 expression in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: HDAC5 inhibitor LMK235 downregulates IL-1β expression in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: Further study detected NFκBIA expression in GNAQ-KO decidual cells treated with HDAC5 inhibitor, LMK235. As shown in Figure 5G, LMK235 significantly rescued the NFκBIA expression in GNAQ-KO decidual cells, downregulated its effectors IL-11 (Figure 5H) and IL-1β (Figure 5I) expression and alleviated the advanced progression of decidualization (Figure 5J) in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 5I shows LMK235 treatment reduces IL-1β expression in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: HDAC5 inhibitor LMK235 alleviates the advanced progression of decidualization in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: Further study detected NFκBIA expression in GNAQ-KO decidual cells treated with HDAC5 inhibitor, LMK235. As shown in Figure 5G, LMK235 significantly rescued the NFκBIA expression in GNAQ-KO decidual cells, downregulated its effectors IL-11 (Figure 5H) and IL-1β (Figure 5I) expression and alleviated the advanced progression of decidualization (Figure 5J) in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 5J shows LMK235 treatment reduces IGFBP-1 expression in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: PMA treatment significantly increases IκBα expression in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: Moreover, to further confirm this assumption, we also detected IκBα expression in PMA or CID755673-treated GNAQ-KO decidual cells. It was found that IκBα expression significantly increased in the PMA-treated GNAQ-KO decidual cells (Figure 5B, C), and CID755673 blocked the IκBα expression (Figure 5C).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 5B, C shows PMA treatment increases IκBα in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: CID755673 blocks IκBα expression in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: Moreover, to further confirm this assumption, we also detected IκBα expression in PMA or CID755673-treated GNAQ-KO decidual cells. It was found that IκBα expression significantly increased in the PMA-treated GNAQ-KO decidual cells (Figure 5B, C), and CID755673 blocked the IκBα expression (Figure 5C).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 5C shows CID755673 treatment blocks IκBα expression.

claim: PKD/PKCμ signaling pathway regulates NFκBIA expression by regulating HDAC5 phosphorylation level and nuclear export during decidualization.
source: Collectively, these results clearly demonstrated that PKD/PKCμ signaling pathway regulated the NFκBIA expression by regulating HDAC5 phosphorylation level and nuclear export during decidualization.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from experiments showing PKD/PKCμ regulates HDAC5 phosphorylation, which affects its nuclear export and consequently NFκBIA expression.

claim: The time required for initiated hatching in the control group was about 8 hr after co-culture (22.2%, 6/27).
source: Results show that, the time required for initiated hatching in the CON group was about 8 hr after co-culture (22.2%, 6/27), whereas the initiation of human blastocyst hatching deferred in the GNAQ-KO (3.7%, 1/27) (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: Co-culture assay data in Figure 6A-C shows blastocyst hatching timing and rate in control group.

claim: The initiation of human blastocyst hatching is deferred in the GNAQ-KO group (3.7%, 1/27) at 8 hr after co-culture.
source: Results show that, the time required for initiated hatching in the CON group was about 8 hr after co-culture (22.2%, 6/27), whereas the initiation of human blastocyst hatching deferred in the GNAQ-KO (3.7%, 1/27) (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: Co-culture assay data in Figure 6A-C shows delayed blastocyst hatching in GNAQ-KO group.

claim: The speed and areas of human blastocyst outgrowth in control group are faster and larger than in GNAQ-KO group at the same co-culture time.
source: The speed and areas of human blastocyst outgrowth in CON group were faster and larger than in GNAQ-KO group at the same co-culture time (Figure 6A, B), corresponding the adhesion rate was notably higher in the CON than in the GNAQ-KO group (29.6%, 8/27 and 11.1%, 3/27, respectively) after co-culture for 72 hr (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: Co-culture assay images in Figure 6A, B show differences in blastocyst outgrowth between groups.

claim: The adhesion rate is notably higher in the control group (29.6%, 8/27) than in the GNAQ-KO group (11.1%, 3/27) after co-culture for 72 hr.
source: The speed and areas of human blastocyst outgrowth in CON group were faster and larger than in GNAQ-KO group at the same co-culture time (Figure 6A, B), corresponding the adhesion rate was notably higher in the CON than in the GNAQ-KO group (29.6%, 8/27 and 11.1%, 3/27, respectively) after co-culture for 72 hr (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: Co-culture assay data in Figure 6A-C shows adhesion rates in both groups.

claim: The over-active inflammation status of GNAQ-KO decidua leads to deferred human blastocyst initiation hatching, arrested outgrowth, and/or failed adhesion.
source: All of these suggested that the over-active inflammation status of GNAQ-KO decidua led to the deferred human blastocyst initiation hatching, arrested outgrowth, and/or failed adhesion.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the co-culture assay data showing impaired blastocyst hatching and adhesion when co-cultured with GNAQ-KO decidual cells.

claim: Endometrial Gαq mRNA level is significantly lower in RPL samples than in normal samples during the first trimester.
source: By comparing the Gαq mRNA and protein levels in decidua tissue between 13 women with normal pregnancy and 13 with RPL, we found that the endometrial Gαq level was significantly lower in RPL samples than in normal samples (Figure 7A–C), IL-11, IL-1β mRNA, and protein or IL-6 mRNA expression were significantly higher in the RPL samples than in the normal samples during the first trimester (Figure 7D–I), consistent with our in vitro studies.
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 7C shows lower GNAQ mRNA in RPL samples compared to normal.

claim: Endometrial Gαq protein level is significantly lower in RPL samples than in normal samples during the first trimester.
source: By comparing the Gαq mRNA and protein levels in decidua tissue between 13 women with normal pregnancy and 13 with RPL, we found that the endometrial Gαq level was significantly lower in RPL samples than in normal samples (Figure 7A–C), IL-11, IL-1β mRNA, and protein or IL-6 mRNA expression were significantly higher in the RPL samples than in the normal samples during the first trimester (Figure 7D–I), consistent with our in vitro studies.
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 7A, B shows lower Gαq protein in RPL samples compared to normal.

claim: IL-11 mRNA expression is significantly higher in RPL samples than in normal samples during the first trimester.
source: By comparing the Gαq mRNA and protein levels in decidua tissue between 13 women with normal pregnancy and 13 with RPL, we found that the endometrial Gαq level was significantly lower in RPL samples than in normal samples (Figure 7A–C), IL-11, IL-1β mRNA, and protein or IL-6 mRNA expression were significantly higher in the RPL samples than in the normal samples during the first trimester (Figure 7D–I), consistent with our in vitro studies.
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 7G, H shows higher IL-11 in RPL samples.

claim: IL-1β mRNA expression is significantly higher in RPL samples than in normal samples during the first trimester.
source: By comparing the Gαq mRNA and protein levels in decidua tissue between 13 women with normal pregnancy and 13 with RPL, we found that the endometrial Gαq level was significantly lower in RPL samples than in normal samples (Figure 7A–C), IL-11, IL-1β mRNA, and protein or IL-6 mRNA expression were significantly higher in the RPL samples than in the normal samples during the first trimester (Figure 7D–I), consistent with our in vitro studies.
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 7F shows higher IL-1β mRNA in RPL samples.

claim: IL-1β protein expression is significantly higher in RPL samples than in normal samples during the first trimester.
source: By comparing the Gαq mRNA and protein levels in decidua tissue between 13 women with normal pregnancy and 13 with RPL, we found that the endometrial Gαq level was significantly lower in RPL samples than in normal samples (Figure 7A–C), IL-11, IL-1β mRNA, and protein or IL-6 mRNA expression were significantly higher in the RPL samples than in the normal samples during the first trimester (Figure 7D–I), consistent with our in vitro studies.
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 7D, E shows higher IL-1β protein in RPL samples.

claim: IL-6 mRNA expression is significantly higher in RPL samples than in normal samples during the first trimester.
source: By comparing the Gαq mRNA and protein levels in decidua tissue between 13 women with normal pregnancy and 13 with RPL, we found that the endometrial Gαq level was significantly lower in RPL samples than in normal samples (Figure 7A–C), IL-11, IL-1β mRNA, and protein or IL-6 mRNA expression were significantly higher in the RPL samples than in the normal samples during the first trimester (Figure 7D–I), consistent with our in vitro studies.
evidence: qRT-PCR data in Figure 7I shows higher IL-6 mRNA in RPL samples.

claim: Abnormal endometrial Gαq expression contributes to recurrent pregnancy loss.
source: Our novel findings collectively suggested that abnormal endometrial Gαq expression contribute to RPL.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from clinical data showing lower Gαq and higher inflammatory cytokines in RPL samples, consistent with in vitro findings.

claim: Decidualization is a prerequisite for normal embryo implantation and successful pregnancy in humans.
source: Decidualization, denoting the transformation of endometrial stromal cells into specialized decidual cells, is a prerequisite for normal embryo implantation and a successful pregnancy in human.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about decidualization's role in pregnancy.

claim: Knockout of Gαq leads to an aberrantly enhanced inflammatory state during decidualization.
source: Here, we demonstrated that knockout of Gαq lead to an aberrantly enhanced inflammatory state during decidualization.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by multiple experimental findings throughout the manuscript showing increased inflammatory markers in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: Deficiency of Gαq results in over-activation of NF-κB signaling due to decreased expression of NFκBIA.
source: Furthermore, we showed that deficiency of Gαq resulted in over-activation of nuclear factor (NF)-κB signaling, due to the decreased expression of NFκBIA, which encode the IκB protein and is the negative regulator for NF-κB.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by experimental data showing decreased NFκBIA and increased NF-κB activity in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: NFκBIA encodes the IκB protein and is the negative regulator for NF-κB.
source: Furthermore, we showed that deficiency of Gαq resulted in over-activation of nuclear factor (NF)-κB signaling, due to the decreased expression of NFκBIA, which encode the IκB protein and is the negative regulator for NF-κB.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the relationship between NFκBIA and NF-κB signaling.

claim: Gαq deficiency decreases PKD phosphorylation levels.
source: Mechanistically, Gαq deficiency decreased the Protein kinase D (PKD, also called PKCμ) phosphorylation levels, leading to attenuated HDAC5 phosphorylation and thus its nuclear export.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by western blot data showing reduced p-PKD in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: Decreased PKD phosphorylation leads to attenuated HDAC5 phosphorylation and nuclear export.
source: Mechanistically, Gαq deficiency decreased the Protein kinase D (PKD, also called PKCμ) phosphorylation levels, leading to attenuated HDAC5 phosphorylation and thus its nuclear export.
evidence: This is a mechanistic claim supported by experimental data showing the relationship between PKD and HDAC5 phosphorylation.

claim: Aberrantly high level of nuclear HDAC5 retards histone acetylation to inhibit induced NFκBIA transcription during decidualization.
source: Aberrantly high level of nuclear HDAC5 retarded histone acetylation to inhibit the induced NFκBIA transcription during decidualization.
evidence: This is a mechanistic claim supported by ChIP data showing HDAC5 binding to NFκBIA promoter and rescue experiments with HDAC5 inhibitor.

claim: Pharmacological activation of PKD/PKCμ restores the inflammatory state and proper decidual response in Gαq-deficient cells.
source: Consistently, pharmacological activation of the PKD/PKCμ or inhibition of the HDAC5 restored the inflammatory state and proper decidual response.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by rescue experiments using PMA activator.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of HDAC5 restores the inflammatory state and proper decidual response in Gαq-deficient cells.
source: Consistently, pharmacological activation of the PKD/PKCμ or inhibition of the HDAC5 restored the inflammatory state and proper decidual response.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by rescue experiments using LMK235 inhibitor.

claim: Over-active inflammatory state in Gαq-deficient decidua defers blastocyst hatching and adhesion in vitro.
source: Finally, we disclosed that over-active inflammatory state in Gαq-deficient decidua deferred the blastocyst hatching and adhesion in vitro, and the decidual expression of Gαq was significantly lower in women with recurrent pregnancy loss compared with normal pregnancy.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by co-culture assay data.

claim: Decidual expression of Gαq is significantly lower in women with recurrent pregnancy loss compared with normal pregnancy.
source: Finally, we disclosed that over-active inflammatory state in Gαq-deficient decidua deferred the blastocyst hatching and adhesion in vitro, and the decidual expression of Gαq was significantly lower in women with recurrent pregnancy loss compared with normal pregnancy.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by clinical sample analysis data.

claim: Successful pregnancy requires precisely coordinated immune responses between the mother and fetus.
source: Successful pregnancy requires precisely coordinated immune responses between the mother and fetus (Yockey and Iwasaki, 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Disorders in maternal-fetal immune communications are tightly associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes including recurrent pregnancy loss.
source: Disorders in these communications are tightly associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes including recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) (Wu et al., 2018; Yockey and Iwasaki, 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Compromised inflammatory cytokine expression in the endometrium has been demonstrated in RPL patients.
source: Increasing evidence has demonstrated compromised inflammatory cytokine expression in the endometrium from RPL patients (Wu et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Cytokine signaling pathways participate in the differentiation of endometrium to promote healthy pregnancy.
source: Cytokine signaling pathways participate the differentiation of endometrium to promote healthy pregnancy, for their ability to drastically alter cellular function, cell–cell communication, and gene expression (Vinketova et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Dysregulated or inappropriately expressed cytokines during inflammation have the potential to act as teratogens and disrupt fetal and placental development.
source: However, when dysregulated or inappropriately expressed during the inflammation, cytokines have the potential to act as teratogens and disrupt fetal and placental developmental, leading to birth defects and pregnancy complications (Yockey and Iwasaki, 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Cyclic decidualization is crucial for embryo implantation and human reproductive success.
source: Cyclic decidualization, formed during the secretory phase of menstrual cycle from uterine mucosa termed endometrium, is crucial for embryo implantation and human reproductive success (Gellersen and Brosens, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Decidual stromal cells differentiate from endometrial stromal cells under the influence of ovarian hormones and cyclic adenosine monophosphate.
source: Decidual stromal cells (DSCs) differentiate from endometrial stromal cells (ESCs) under the influence of ovarian hormones and cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the process of decidualization.

claim: Decidual transformation of ESCs involves genome-wide remodeling of the chromatin landscape.
source: At the molecular level, decidual transformation of ESCs involves genome-wide remodeling of the chromatin landscape (Vrljicak et al., 2018), wholesale reprogramming of several signaling pathways (Cloke et al., 2008; Leitao et al., 2010), including progesterone and cAMP/protein kinase A (PKA) signaling pathways.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Decidual transformation involves wholesale reprogramming of several signaling pathways including progesterone and cAMP/PKA signaling pathways.
source: At the molecular level, decidual transformation of ESCs involves genome-wide remodeling of the chromatin landscape (Vrljicak et al., 2018), wholesale reprogramming of several signaling pathways (Cloke et al., 2008; Leitao et al., 2010), including progesterone and cAMP/protein kinase A (PKA) signaling pathways.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Gαq belongs to the Gq/11 subfamily of heterotrimeric G proteins and is ubiquitously expressed in mammalian cells.
source: Gαq, encoded by the GNAQ gene, belongs to the Gq/11 subfamily of heterotrimeric G proteins, and it is ubiquitously expressed in mammalian cells (Wilkie et al., 1991).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Gαq links GPCRs to activate Phospholipase C that hydrolyzes PIP2 to release IP3 and DAG.
source: The Gαq links GPCRs to activate Phospholipase C (PLC) that hydrolyzes membrane phospholipids phosphatidylinositol bisphosphate, PIP2 to release inositol trisphosphate (IP3) and diacylglycerol (DAG) – two important second messengers causing Ca2+ mobilization and protein kinase C (PKC) activation (Ho et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Gαq signaling supported by citation to previous study.

claim: IP3 and DAG are important second messengers causing Ca2+ mobilization and protein kinase C activation.
source: The Gαq links GPCRs to activate Phospholipase C (PLC) that hydrolyzes membrane phospholipids phosphatidylinositol bisphosphate, PIP2 to release inositol trisphosphate (IP3) and diacylglycerol (DAG) – two important second messengers causing Ca2+ mobilization and protein kinase C (PKC) activation (Ho et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge about second messenger signaling supported by citation.

claim: HESC usually stops proliferating on the fourth day of decidual induction.
source: According to previous studies, HESC usually stopped proliferating on the fourth day of decidual induction (Jiang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Wnt signaling pathway has been reported to regulate stromal apoptosis and differentiation during decidualization.
source: Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis revealed that most top-ranked biological processes included the Wnt signaling pathway (Sharma et al., 2016; Pathak et al., 2021) and JAK–STAT, NF-κB inflammation pathway (Figure 1F, G), which had been reported to regulate stromal apoptosis and differentiation during the decidualization, the latter consistent with the notions regarding the role of Gαq during immune regulation (Wang et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: JAK-STAT and NF-κB inflammation pathways have been reported to regulate stromal apoptosis and differentiation during decidualization.
source: Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis revealed that most top-ranked biological processes included the Wnt signaling pathway (Sharma et al., 2016; Pathak et al., 2021) and JAK–STAT, NF-κB inflammation pathway (Figure 1F, G), which had been reported to regulate stromal apoptosis and differentiation during the decidualization, the latter consistent with the notions regarding the role of Gαq during immune regulation (Wang et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Gαq has been reported to play a role in immune regulation.
source: Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis revealed that most top-ranked biological processes included the Wnt signaling pathway (Sharma et al., 2016; Pathak et al., 2021) and JAK–STAT, NF-κB inflammation pathway (Figure 1F, G), which had been reported to regulate stromal apoptosis and differentiation during the decidualization, the latter consistent with the notions regarding the role of Gαq during immune regulation (Wang et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Inactivated NF-κB is anchored to inhibitor κBα (IκBα) in the cytosol.
source: It has been reported that inactivation NF-κB is anchored to inhibitor κBα (IκBα) in the cytosol.
evidence: This is established knowledge about NF-κB regulation.

claim: Upon IκBα phosphorylation by IKK, it undergoes ubiquitin-dependent degradation.
source: Upon IκBα phosphorylated by IκB kinase (IKK), it undergoes ubiquitin-dependent degradation (Maniatis, 1997), and the 'free' NF-κB then translocates into the nucleus to induces numerous NF-κB targeted inflammatory gene transcriptions.
evidence: This is established knowledge about NF-κB activation supported by citation.

claim: Free NF-κB translocates into the nucleus to induce numerous NF-κB targeted inflammatory gene transcriptions.
source: Upon IκBα phosphorylated by IκB kinase (IKK), it undergoes ubiquitin-dependent degradation (Maniatis, 1997), and the 'free' NF-κB then translocates into the nucleus to induces numerous NF-κB targeted inflammatory gene transcriptions.
evidence: This is established knowledge about NF-κB function.

claim: G proteins and their downstream effectors have been found in the nucleus.
source: Previous studies have shown that G proteins, and their downstream effector that are found in the nucleus (Spiegelberg and Hamm, 2005; Campden et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: EGFR family members and PD-L1 have been documented to be localized in the nucleus.
source: There is a substantial body of evidence documenting other membrane proteins, for example, epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) family members and PD-L1 to be localized in the nucleus (Wang et al., 2010b, Wang et al., 2010c, Yu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Translocation of EGFR family members involves recognition of nuclear localization signal by importin proteins.
source: The translocation of EGFR family members involves the recognition of the nuclear localization signal (NLS) by the nuclear transporter importin proteins, thus directing the proteins transport through the nuclear pore complex to the nucleus (Hsu and Hung, 2007; Wang et al., 2010a; Wang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about nuclear protein translocation supported by citations.

claim: Gαq does not contain a classical nuclear localization signal.
source: Unlike EGFR or PD-L1, Gαq does not contain a classical NLS (data not shown) (Yu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from sequence analysis, with citation to previous study for comparison.

claim: Gαq directly activates PLC β, which generates the second messenger DAG.
source: It is well known that Gαq directly activates PLC β, which generates the second messenger DAG.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Gαq signaling.

claim: DAG activates PKC by binding their C1 domains.
source: DAG activates PKC by binding their C1 domains (Chen et al., 2017) and DAG induces the activation of PKD/PKCμ by PKC-dependent phosphorylation (Wang, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: DAG induces the activation of PKD/PKCμ by PKC-dependent phosphorylation.
source: DAG activates PKC by binding their C1 domains (Chen et al., 2017) and DAG induces the activation of PKD/PKCμ by PKC-dependent phosphorylation (Wang, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: PMA as a PKC agonist at 100 nM concentration can mimic DAG to activate PKC.
source: PMA as a PKC agonist, at the concentration of 100 nM was able to mimics the DAG to activate PKC.
evidence: This is established knowledge about PMA function.

claim: HDACs are universally expressed in ESCs and decidual cells.
source: Previous studies have investigated that HDACs universally expressed in ESCs and decidual cells (Pavličev et al., 2017) which play an important role during decidualization (Sakai et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: HDACs play an important role during decidualization.
source: Previous studies have investigated that HDACs universally expressed in ESCs and decidual cells (Pavličev et al., 2017) which play an important role during decidualization (Sakai et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: HDAC4 and HDAC5 expression have a dramatic change during the transformation of endometrial stromal fibroblasts into secretory decidual cells.
source: However, just HDAC4 and HDAC5 expression have a dramatic change during the transformation of the endometrial stromal fibroblasts into secretory decidual cells (Pavličev et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: HDAC5 belongs to the class IIa HDAC family.
source: HDAC5 belongs to the class IIa HDAC family and phosphorylated form has been known to shuttle between the cytosol and the nucleus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HDAC5 classification.

claim: Phosphorylated HDAC5 shuttles between the cytosol and the nucleus.
source: HDAC5 belongs to the class IIa HDAC family and phosphorylated form has been known to shuttle between the cytosol and the nucleus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HDAC5 localization.

claim: HDAC5 phosphorylation can be regulated by PKD/PKCμ or PKA.
source: HDAC5 phosphorylation can be regulated by PKD/PKCμ or PKA (Cho et al., 2015; Weeks et al., 2017; Pietruczuk et al., 2019), which would promote HDAC5 shuttling to the cytosol and relieve its transcription suppress function.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: HDAC5 phosphorylation promotes HDAC5 shuttling to the cytosol and relieves its transcription suppression function.
source: HDAC5 phosphorylation can be regulated by PKD/PKCμ or PKA (Cho et al., 2015; Weeks et al., 2017; Pietruczuk et al., 2019), which would promote HDAC5 shuttling to the cytosol and relieve its transcription suppress function.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: PKD/PKCμ can serve as a HDAC5 kinase downstream of Gαq activation in decidual cells.
source: Our results demonstrate that PKD/PKCμ can serve as a HDAC5 kinase downstream of Gαq activation in decidual cells.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from experimental data showing Gαq regulates PKD/PKCμ phosphorylation, which in turn regulates HDAC5 phosphorylation.

claim: Both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines are potentially required to maintain normal pre-implantation embryo development and blastocyst hatching.
source: Both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokine (of endometrial and embryonic origin) are potentially required to maintain normal pre-implantation embryo development and blastocyst hatching, leading to successful implantation (Pathak et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Deferred or failed blastocyst hatching can lead to blastocyst implantation failure.
source: Deferred or failed blastocyst hatching can lead to blastocyst implantation failure (Khorram et al., 2000), and delayed or failed blastocyst adhesion miss the 'implantation window' lead to infertility or early pregnancy loss.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Delayed or failed blastocyst adhesion missing the implantation window leads to infertility or early pregnancy loss.
source: Deferred or failed blastocyst hatching can lead to blastocyst implantation failure (Khorram et al., 2000), and delayed or failed blastocyst adhesion miss the 'implantation window' lead to infertility or early pregnancy loss.
evidence: This is established knowledge about implantation timing.

claim: Decidual secretions contain high amounts of inflammatory cytokines including IL-1β, IL-6, and IL-11.
source: The decidual secretions contain high amounts inflammatory cytokine that include IL-1β, IL-6, and IL-11 (White et al., 2007; Sharma et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Excessively elevated levels of inflammatory cytokines likely induce ER stress in invading EVTs.
source: But, excessively elevated levels of inflammatory cytokine likely induce ER stress in the invading EVTs (Lee et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Early decidualization inflammatory state is dominated by STAT signaling.
source: Transcriptional patterns suggested that the early decidualization inflammatory state is dominated by STAT signaling.
evidence: This is established knowledge about decidualization phases.

claim: In late phase decidualization, STATs are downregulated and transcription of NF-κB repressors decreases, possibly leading to NF-κB pathway activation.
source: In the late phase, however, STATs are downregulated and the transcription of NF-κB repressors decreases, possibly leading to NF-κB pathway activation (Rytkönen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Gαq activation is sufficient to stimulate sustained PKD activation via PKC.
source: It has been reported that Gαq activation is sufficient to stimulate sustained PKD activation via PKC (Yuan et al., 2000), but we detected no significant alteration in the phosphorylation of PKCα/β (Figure 5—figure supplements 1A and 2A), indicating that this PKC activation is not sufficient for PKD phosphorylation in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation, but the authors note their data shows this pathway may not be active in their system.

claim: PKC activation via the canonical pathway is not sufficient for PKD phosphorylation in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
source: It has been reported that Gαq activation is sufficient to stimulate sustained PKD activation via PKC (Yuan et al., 2000), but we detected no significant alteration in the phosphorylation of PKCα/β (Figure 5—figure supplements 1A and 2A), indicating that this PKC activation is not sufficient for PKD phosphorylation in GNAQ-KO decidual cells.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the observation that PKCα/β phosphorylation is not altered in GNAQ-KO cells despite reduced PKD phosphorylation.

claim: G-protein Gs couples many receptors to adenylyl cyclase and mediates receptor-dependent adenylyl cyclase activation.
source: The G-protein adenylyl cyclase stimulatory G protein (Gs) couples many receptors to adenylyl cyclase and mediates receptor-dependent adenylyl cyclase activation, resulting in increasing level of intracellular cAMP to activate PKA to regulate the expression of major decidual factors.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Gs signaling.

claim: Gs activation results in increasing levels of intracellular cAMP to activate PKA to regulate the expression of major decidual factors.
source: The G-protein adenylyl cyclase stimulatory G protein (Gs) couples many receptors to adenylyl cyclase and mediates receptor-dependent adenylyl cyclase activation, resulting in increasing level of intracellular cAMP to activate PKA to regulate the expression of major decidual factors.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cAMP/PKA signaling in decidualization.

claim: There may be PKC-independent pathways stimulated by Gαq that are responsible for PKD/PKCμ activation during decidualization.
source: These findings revealed that Gαq stimulate PKD/PKCμ activation may not via protein kinase C during decidualization, and suggest that there may be PKC-independent pathways stimulated by Gαq that are responsible for PKD/PKCμ activation during decidualization.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion drawn from the observation that PKCα/β is not altered in GNAQ-KO cells.

claim: Phosphorylated HDAC5 stimulates its nuclear export.
source: Phosphorylated HDAC5 could stimulate its nuclear export (Weeks et al., 2017; Pietruczuk et al., 2019), and HDAC5 nuclear export enhances histone acetylation to activate the target gene expression (Cho et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: HDAC5 nuclear export enhances histone acetylation to activate target gene expression.
source: Phosphorylated HDAC5 could stimulate its nuclear export (Weeks et al., 2017; Pietruczuk et al., 2019), and HDAC5 nuclear export enhances histone acetylation to activate the target gene expression (Cho et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: For a successful early pregnancy, proper decidualization with homeostasis of cytokine secretome governed by Gαq is pre-requisite.
source: Based on these finding, we demonstrated that, for a successful early pregnancy, a proper decidualization with homeostasis of cytokines secretome govern by Gαq is pre-requested, which provided a new hint for understanding the early pregnancy loss.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from all experimental findings in the study.

claim: STAT3 is maximally expressed in decidual cells during late-secretory phase.
source: STAT3 is maximally expressed in decidual cells during late-secretory phase (Dimitriadis et al., 2006), phosphorylated STAT3 is the activated form of STAT3 and is the convergent downstream effector of IL-11 (Taniguchi and Karin, 2014; Heichler et al., 2020) and IL-1β (Yao et al., 2017) signaling.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: The receptors of prokineticin-1, relaxin, and PGE2 are G-protein-coupled receptors characterized by seven transmembrane spanning domains.
source: The receptors of prokineticin-1, relaxin, and PGE2 are G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) characterized by the presence of seven transmembrane spanning domains (Cook et al., 2010) that are primarily considered to couple Gαs to activate adenylate cyclase that subsequently forms the second messenger cAMP.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Prokineticin-1, relaxin, and PGE2 receptors primarily couple Gαs to activate adenylate cyclase that subsequently forms cAMP.
source: The receptors of prokineticin-1, relaxin, and PGE2 are G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) characterized by the presence of seven transmembrane spanning domains (Cook et al., 2010) that are primarily considered to couple Gαs to activate adenylate cyclase that subsequently forms the second messenger cAMP.
evidence: This is established knowledge about GPCR signaling.

claim: cAMP signaling participates in decidualization by activation of PKA to influence the expression of major decidual factors including PRL and IGFBP-1.
source: cAMP signaling participates the decidualization by the activation of PKA to influence the expression of major decidual factors, including prolactin (PRL) (Telgmann et al., 1997) and insulin-like growth factor-binding protein-1 (IGFBP-1) (Tamura et al., 2012), two specific markers of ESC decidualization.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: PRL and IGFBP-1 are two specific markers of ESC decidualization.
source: cAMP signaling participates the decidualization by the activation of PKA to influence the expression of major decidual factors, including prolactin (PRL) (Telgmann et al., 1997) and insulin-like growth factor-binding protein-1 (IGFBP-1) (Tamura et al., 2012), two specific markers of ESC decidualization.
evidence: This is established knowledge about decidualization markers.
